verdict: Elevance Health grew total revenue 1.4% to $51.4B and lifted EPS 18% to $6.27, as medical costs ran better than a year ago and investment income jumped — even though membership shrank — and it raised its full-year guidance.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Total revenue was $51.4B; operating revenue was $50.4B, up 0.7%

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $5.32 a year ago; adjusted diluted EPS was $6.99

kpis.label: Benefit expense ratio
kpis.note: Share of premiums paid out as medical care — improved from 91.3% a year ago

kpis.label: Medical membership
kpis.note: People covered — down 487,000 from a year ago, mainly in Medicare Advantage and Medicaid

segments.name: Premiums
segments.note: Health-insurance premiums from members, employers and government programs — the money people pay for coverage. Roughly flat: higher premium rates offset lower Medicare Advantage, Medicaid and employer risk membership. Health Benefits, the insurance segment, had $43.4B of operating revenue.

segments.name: Products
segments.note: Prescription drugs and other products sold, mainly through CarelonRx pharmacies. Carelon, the health-services segment, had $19.3B of operating revenue (before eliminations between segments).

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Fees for care delivery and health services, mainly from Carelon Services.

segments.name: Net investment income & other
segments.note: Income from the company's investment portfolio of $1,037M, less $48M of net losses on financial instruments. Investment income rose 66% from a year ago.

opex.name: Cost of products sold
opex.note: What the company paid for the prescription drugs and products it sold — up 5%, in line with product revenue.

opex.name: Operating expense
opex.note: The day-to-day cost of running the company — people, technology and offices. At 11.4% of operating revenue, up from 10.5%, reflecting targeted one-time investments in new capabilities.

opex.name: Amortization of other intangible assets
opex.note: A non-cash charge spreading the cost of intangible assets from past acquisitions over their useful lives.

follow100Note: Rows may add to $99.99 rather than $100.00 due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Medical costs ran better
takeaways.text: The benefit expense ratio — the share of premiums paid out as medical care — improved to 90.6% from 91.3%, driven by better performance in Medicare Advantage and individual ACA plans. Benefit expense itself fell about 1% to $37.8B even though premiums were flat.

takeaways.title: Fewer members, higher rates
takeaways.text: Medical membership fell to 44.9 million, down 487,000 from a year ago: Medicare Advantage membership dropped 15.5% and Medicaid 4.9%, partly offset by growth in fee-based commercial plans. Operating revenue still rose 0.7% to $50.4B because premium rates and CarelonRx product sales rose.

takeaways.title: Guidance raised on both measures
takeaways.text: GAAP diluted EPS was $6.27, up 18%; adjusted EPS was $6.99. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance to at least $22.00 of diluted EPS and at least $29.00 adjusted, and expects adjusted EPS to grow at least 12% in 2027. Net investment income jumping 66% to $1,037M helped this quarter's result.

oneTimers: Items the company excludes from adjusted results in the quarter: $106M of intangible amortization, $48M of net losses on financial instruments, $42M of transaction and integration costs, $18M of business optimization charges and $8M of litigation and settlement expenses — $155M in total after a $67M tax benefit. Adjusted shareholders' net income was $1,520M vs $1,365M as reported.
otherDetail: Other expense of $358M is interest expense. Investment income is not in this line — it is already counted in revenue.
footerNote: Operating income here ($2,152M) is total revenue less benefit expense, cost of products sold, operating expense and intangible amortization. The company reports 'operating gain' of $1.3B, measured on operating revenue only — it excludes investment income and amortization. Total net income was $1,343M; shareholders' net income was $1,365M, the difference being a $22M loss attributable to noncontrolling interests. Benefit expense (medical claims) plays the role of cost of revenue for a health insurer.
